title: Electricity and Circuits (KS2)
subject: Science
strapline: Making a bulb light — complete circuits, conductors and switches.
facts: A simple circuit needs a cell (battery), wires and a component such as a bulb or buzzer.
A circuit must be complete (an unbroken loop) for electricity to flow and the bulb to light.
A switch works by breaking or completing the circuit to turn things off or on.
A conductor lets electricity flow through it — most metals are good conductors.
An insulator does not let electricity flow — plastic, rubber, wood and glass are insulators.
Adding more cells can make a bulb brighter; a broken wire or loose connection stops the flow.
Mains electricity is powerful and dangerous — only ever use batteries for experiments.

quick_quiz.q: What must a circuit be for the bulb to light?
Is plastic a conductor or an insulator?
What component lets you turn a circuit on and off?

teacher_tips: Build real circuits — the "complete loop" idea rarely lands from a diagram alone.
Test conductors/insulators by putting objects into a working circuit.
Teach circuit symbols alongside the real components.
